To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the W78S and glutamate mutants of NS2/ NEP were important for virus polymerase inhibition and that the glutamine mutants resulted in attenuated virus.

(i) the NS2/ NEP W78S mutant was able to replicate to high titres in MDCK cells and in mice, (ii) the NS2 W67S/W74S/W75S mutant showed reduced polymerase activity, and (iii) the NS1/NS2 double mutant showed attenuated virus growth in mice, suggesting that it could be a potential live vaccine.
We have used reverse genetics to identify NS2 mutants that attenuate influenza viruses in mice, with potential for vaccine development.

the development of novel live attenuated influenza virus vaccines.
the design of attenuated live influenza A vaccines and provides a basis for the development of novel vaccines that may have a broad spectrum of efficacy.

this work has identified a novel mechanism of influenza virus attenuation that could be useful for the design of new live attenuated vaccines.
this paper describes a structure-based design of NS mutations to attenuate the virus.
the W78S and the glutamate triple mutant (E67S/ E74S/E75) are important for the inhibition of influenza viral transcription and replication.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the W78 residue and the C-terminal glutamates are critical for NS2/NEPs ability to inhibit influenza viral polymerase and that NS1-7 mutants with the addition of seven NS2/NEPg amino acids to the NS1 gene are attenuated in vivo.

we have identified the critical role of the NS2-NEP C-terminal domain for virus growth, and that the addition of seven NS amino acids at the C-termini of NS1 may have potential as a strategy to generate a safer influenza A live virus vaccine.
NS2 mutants that disrupt NS2/NEp interaction with M1 can be used for attenuated vaccines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C-termini of NS1 and NS2/NEPs are functionally linked, and that mutations in the C-terminal residues of NS2/ NEP can attenuate influenza virus in mice.
the C-terminal region of NS2 is a potential target for attenuating influenza virus.
NS2/NEPs with mutations at the C-terminal glutamates and W78 are promising vaccine candidates for the development of attenuated live vaccines.
